idea: RE-TARGETED (operator pivot 2026-06-08): make a raw `codex` invocation of OUR FORK binary behave EXACTLY like `happy codex` -- full mobile remote control (turns, approvals, interrupt/stop) + discoverable + synced -- by INTEGRATING the Happy client NATIVELY INTO THE FORK, ideally with NO happy-cli runtime dependency (codex-rs -> happy-server directly). Not read-only, not a PATH alias. The prior read-only mirror (D-001 @ e27720bc) is demoted to the degraded fallback only.

candidateDirections.name: B -- Native Rust Happy session client overlay crate (codex-happy), session-scope first
candidateDirections.summary: New conflict-free `codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy` crate ports the Happy PROTOCOL client to Rust (TweetNaCl-equivalent crypto + Socket.IO /v1/updates + happy-wire session schemas + getOrCreateSession + GitHub device-flow/Dev-Tunnels auth), driven by a BOUNDED, registered, rebase-gated upstream-canonical control seam in tui (AppEvent/AppCommand) + core/session (event fan-out from the single-consumer mpsc) so one raw `codex` self-connects with NO happy-cli runtime process. NOT overlay-only and NOT launcher-wired (launcher execs codex-core then exits). Effort XL.

candidateDirections.name: D -- Hybrid: native in-fork control seam + retained happy-cli daemon owns Happy wire/keys/machine scope
candidateDirections.summary: Reuse the SAME bounded tui/core control seam as B, but the Happy protocol/E2EE/Socket.IO/machine-RPCs stay in the proven TypeScript happy-cli daemon, reached over a thin local IPC. Avoids the second crypto/Socket.IO/wire implementation and keeps Happy egress out of the audited codex-core, at the cost of a happy-cli runtime dependency the operator wants to remove. The principled fallback if the native-Rust protocol round-trip proves too costly; also the natural home for machine-level scope. Effort L.

candidateDirections.name: A -- Launcher-internal delegation: codex.exe re-execs into the existing `happy codex` path
candidateDirections.summary: Inside codex.exe (not a user PATH alias), detect Happy availability and re-exec into `happy codex`, reusing runCodex/CodexAppServerClient/ApiSessionClient verbatim for exact parity. Lowest engineering risk but KEEPS the happy-cli runtime dependency and preserves the very app-server JSON-RPC driver layer the operator wants to collapse. Keep only as a safety valve / transitional fallback, with recursion + double-wrap guards. Effort M.

candidateDirections.name: C -- Fork-bundled thin Happy bridge sidecar auto-started by codex
candidateDirections.summary: The fork bundles and auto-starts a minimal Happy-protocol bridge process; codex-rs talks to it over a small local IPC. Middle ground between B (no extra process, full Rust port) and A/D (full happy-cli). Risk: the bridge accretes key ownership, Socket.IO state, RPC routing and lifecycle until it is a second happy-cli daemon in practice, undermining the operator's direct-to-happy-server goal. Effort L.

questionsForSynthesis: v1 scope: stop at SESSION-LEVEL parity (tree visibility + encrypted sync + mobile turns + live config + approvals + interrupt/stop) and DEFER machine-level (machine presence, spawn-from-mobile, fork-into-worktree, keepalive)? All three lenses recommend yes.

PHASE-0 SPIKE (gate before committing to B's full port): can a bounded upstream-canonical seam expose a complete turn/approval/interrupt/stop tap+inject over the TUI AppEvent/AppCommand layer in few enough patched lines to honor the minimize-conflict-surface tenet (registered in codex docs/implementation/patch-surface.md)? And can a Rust client round-trip POST /v1/sessions (dataKey+legacy), /v3 message send, Socket.IO /v1/updates, and metadata/state CAS against a dev happy-server with NO happy-server protocol changes?

E2EE key ownership: is it acceptable for the integrated `codex` process to read ~/.happy credentials and own per-session data keys, REPLACING the prior daemon-sole-holder model for this path? (codex child already inherits all HAPPY_* env today, same trust boundary -- but this moves key material into the network-audited binary.)

NETWORK-AUDIT surface: B/C add a new happy-server + Dev-Tunnels egress path INSIDE the audited codex-core boundary (scripts/audit_network_calls.sh + runtime_audit.ps1). New allowlist host + patch-surface registration + justification required. Is expanding the fork's audited egress acceptable, or is that itself a reason to keep Happy egress in a separate process (D)?

Idempotency: disable native autoconnect when HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID is present OR the subcommand is `app-server` so an explicit `happy codex` (or its spawned app-server child) does not double-wrap / create duplicate sessions.

Graceful fallback: no creds / not authed / offline -> silent vanilla `codex` within a strict startup-latency budget; optionally fall through to the prior D-001 read-only daemon mirror as a lesser degraded mode when a daemon is present.

Opt-in/config: build-time default-on with a kill switch (~/.codex-copilot/config.toml + env), since this is OUR build; mirror the existing launcher-config pattern (style_user_messages / auto_load_claude_md).

Maintenance: is eliminating the happy-cli runtime dependency worth maintaining a SECOND protocol implementation (Rust Socket.IO + NaCl-compatible crypto + AES-GCM dataKey + Ed25519 auth + happy-wire schemas + metadata CAS + reconnect) in parallel with the TypeScript @slopus/happy-wire as both evolve?
